source_inventory.classification_notes: Stage 6 has 38 numbered footnotes in the value chain and additional sub-citations in the pain-points document. Many footnotes bundle 2–4 URLs. Each URL is classified independently. Several critical sources are tagged [NEEDS-ATTENDED-FETCH] (OJK Roadmap PDF; AGCS Annual Report PDF). Vendor-self-citation pattern is materially lower than Stage 3: most vendor claims (Parsyl, Overhaul, Loadsure, Cover Genius) are anchored to press releases for funding claims rather than product-capability claims sourced from vendor pages — however PR Newswire and company websites still appear as the primary source for several material claims. The dominant primary anchor sources are: IUMI Stats Report 2025 (primary_association — cited 7+ times across both documents), Tokio Marine Holdings FY2024 4Q Summary Report (primary_filing), Munich Re Group Annual Report 2024 (primary_filing), Crawford NYSE audited results (primary_filing), and BSI/TT Club 2024 Cargo Theft Report (primary_association). These are all legitimate primary-tier sources. The main source-quality problems in this stage are: (a) cargo theft statistics from Overhaul's own press releases (auto-low-vendor for the company's own incident-count reports), (b) a Dataintelo APAC market size figure (aggregator auto-downgrade), (c) a 12% IoT loss ratio reduction figure from Astute Analytica/GlobeNewswire (aggregator auto-downgrade), (d) TruckerCloud blog for 8-day FNOL gap (auto-low-vendor or at best single secondary-trade), (e) strategic theft 1,455% growth figure traced to Travelers Insurance (auto-low-vendor), (f) Verisk CargoNet figures (primary_association — acceptable), and (g) multiple claims with [ASSUMED-N] tags properly flagged in the draft.

gate_reasoning: Stage 6 exhibits a strong primary-source foundation for its most critical market-sizing and carrier financial claims: IUMI Stats Report 2025 (primary_association), Tokio Marine Holdings 4Q FY2024 Summary Report (primary_filing), Munich Re Group Annual Report 2024 (primary_filing), Crawford NYSE audited results (primary_filing), BSI/TT Club 2024 and 2025 Cargo Theft Reports (primary_association), and Verisk CargoNet 2024/2025 annual reports (primary_association) collectively cover the headline market figures at High or Medium confidence. The stage correctly identifies and tags seven [ASSUMED-N] claims that are internally generated and not evidenced — these are properly disclosed and do not inflate the scoring. The scoring distribution (36% High / 36% Medium / 28% Low) is materially better than Stage 3's distribution and reflects a research pass where the author exercised reasonable source discipline on the primary metrics. However, three significant source-quality problems require flagging before shipping: (1) Overhaul's H1 2024 Cargo Theft Report — sourced from Overhaul's own press release — is cited as foundational evidence across both documents (four distinct claim instances) for the severity of cargo theft and Overhaul's own product performance; independent CargoNet or NICB cross-validation of the 49%/+83% YoY figures is missing and must be obtained in deep research before these statistics can be stated without caveat; (2) the underinsurance rate (60–90%) traces entirely to Loadsure's own marketing claims with no independent primary study, yet is cited as a structural market characterization in PP6.3; (3) the TruckerCloud 8-day FNOL gap claim is vendor self-interest sourcing for a foundational pain point. One factual-inaccuracy flag (Otonomi '22x faster' calculation error vs. stated 48h/30-day comparison = 15x) should be resolved. The Tokio Marine SEA operational footprint (10,000+ employees, 8 P&C subsidiaries) is sourced only from Tokio Marine's own marketing pages — for a document directly relevant to a Tokio Marine venture pitch, this specific claim needs audited or regulatory corroboration. Deep research should address the top 3 weak claims before final compilation.
